findings.surface: EventBridge->SQS delivery and dead-letter writes; SNS->SQS; S3->SQS validation; Lambda SQS event source mappings; SES S3 receipt rule; CloudTrail bucket policy
findings.claim: A queue/resource policy combining an Allow for the service principal with the standard enforceSSL Deny (Bool aws:SecureTransport=false, CDK enforceSSL / DenyInsecureTransport) is treated as a refusal by every service-to-service policy pre-check at fork head. EventBridge's queue_delivery_refusal builds an iam_authorization::Request whose context and published keys are only aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount; the shared evaluator is fail-closed on condition keys it does not model (an undecided Deny still refuses), so an event over the emulator's HTTPS/in-process transport is withheld just as a plaintext request would be. EventBridge-specific runtime witness is NOT in the corpus; the sibling paths have runtime repros in gh#369, gh#409, gh#447, gh#451, gh#459.

findings.surface: SQS queue policy evaluation for in-process cross-service delivery
findings.claim: SQS itself cannot enforce a queue resource policy on a cross-service delivery. The in-process SDK client signs with the emulator's own callback credential; STS resolves any unrecognized access key to the ambient/account-root identity, and SQS's authorize() short-circuits to Ok for that identity. The service-principal call directory that SNS mints for its fan-out is consulted by SQS only to relax MaximumMessageSize, never for authorization. Producers therefore each duplicate the queue-policy decision (EventBridge queue_delivery_refusal, SNS resource_policy_allows, S3 destination_granted, Lambda read_is_withheld), and those copies diverge (EF-01, EF-03). EventBridgeV2 and Pipes skip the check entirely (EF-06).
findings.root_cause: No single service-principal-aware authorization gate for cross-service sends: credentials, not the recorded ServicePrincipalCall, decide the caller; the account credential is an unconditional allow.

findings.claim: After ~15 minutes without writes, a DynamoDB-stream->SQS pipe hits ExpiredIteratorException on every poll; records written during the failure window are not delivered, DescribePipe still says RUNNING, and nothing reaches the DLQ. Stop/StartPipe does not help on 1.0.518; on 1.0.531 the run recovered after ~2 minutes but the failing window was untested. Head code confirms the reporter's source reading: collect_stream_batch continues on an empty GetRecords without storing NextShardIterator (also inside its batching loop), while GetRecords mints a fresh iterator on EVERY read and the streams service retires the oldest live iterator at 10,000 and expires iterators at 15 minutes. The Kinesis source deliberately holds a POSITION instead, with a comment describing exactly this failure mode.
findings.root_cause: StreamCursors holds an opaque, short-lived iterator token rather than a durable position; an empty read does not advance it, so idle polls reuse an iterator that the DDB Streams service has already retired/aged out.

findings.root_cause: The open-doc corpus is a moving ledger: docs are identified against older commits and are not re-replayed/pruned when code changes, so a keyword count over claims.jsonl overstates live divergences and can contain mutually contradictory AWS expectations.

gaps: No emulator/CLI runtime execution and no independent AWS calls were performed in this audit. Every AWS-behavior statement is quoted from an in-repo simparity-behavioral-aws-v1 / simparity-wire-aws-v1 witness or a GitHub issue repro; those are not independently verified here.
The LinkedIn '0 of 3' event-flow claim (linkedin-post.txt:21) cannot be graded: the three checks are not enumerated and no matching 3-check report exists in the corpus. No parity conclusion is drawn.

The EventBridge->SQS enforceSSL/DenyInsecureTransport failure (EF-01) is a code-level inference from the shared IAM evaluator; there is NO EventBridge-specific runtime witness in census.json/claims.jsonl. A replay with a queue policy containing Bool aws:SecureTransport=false plus an Allow for events.amazonaws.com is required.

A large fraction of the 5,355 open docs were written against older commits. At least 27 ESM-never-delivers docs, 31 NonExistentQueue/WSDL docs, 20261029T182228Z-events-eventbridge-does-not-authorize-sqs-targets-against-the.md, and 20261115T165530Z-sns-nothing-is-ever-posted-to-an-https.md are contradicted by head code; 20261115T153528Z and 20261111T033241Z disagree on the expected DLQ ERROR_CODE. 20261116T144630Z-sqs-the-eventbridgev2-subscriber-delivery-never-raises-queue.md explicitly labels its delivery-leg cause an unverified hypothesis with an upstream CreateEventBus 400; head code has subscriber_delivery::send_to_queue. Do not close that claim either way without a replay.

Only claims.jsonl rows (572 GH + 5,355 open docs + 7,114 stubs) were counted; the 7,114 stub rows were not audited for event-delivery completeness, and composite docs with 'N net-new causes' were counted as one row even when only one cause belongs to a root cause.

The '0/3' and 'EventBridge->SQS' shorthand may refer to different services (EventBridge v1 vs EventBridgeV2 vs Pipes). EF-06 shows they behave differently at head: v1 enforces the queue policy, v2 does not.
No parity is claimed: 5,355 open in-repo issue docs remain (111 CRITICAL, 3,888 HIGH) and 17,671 fixed docs do not establish parity.
